mekayis.metin: (خَفَجَ) الْخَاءُ وَالْفَاءُ وَالْجِيمُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى خِلَافِ الِاسْتِقَامَةِ. فَالْأَخْفَجُ: الْأَعْوَجُ الرِّجْلِ ; وَالْمَصْدَرُ الْخَفَجُ، وَيُقَالُ إِنَّ الْخَفَجَ الرِّعْدَةُ. وَهُوَ ذَاكَ الْقِيَاسُ.

kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Unknown. According to Dictionnaire du faisceau dialectal arabe andalou, which glosses as wild radish (Raphanus raphanistrum), a homonymic word meaning a foot disease of camels is unrelated and the plant name is rather from Persian خفنج (xafanj, “profit, advantage; delight, blandishment”) due to a use as an appetizing snack. But this is doubtful due to the Bedouin usage.
